quickSummary: Carbocations: sp² planar, 6e⁻, electrophiles, 3°>2°>1°>CH₃⁺, undergo 1,2-shifts. Carbanions: sp³ pyramidal, 8e⁻, nucleophiles, CH₃⁻>1°>2°>3° (no shifts). Free radicals: 7e⁻, paramagnetic, 3°>2°>1°>CH₃⁺ (no shifts).
summary: Master homolytic and heterolytic bond fission, carbocation rearrangements, and relative stabilities of intermediates.

summaryBox.title: 3 Intermediates
summaryBox.takeaway: Carbocation (6e⁻, sp², 3°>2°>1°, 1,2-shifts); Carbanion (8e⁻, sp³, CH₃⁻>1°>2°>3°, no shifts); Radical (7e⁻, sp², 3°>2°>1°, no shifts).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
REACTIVE INTERMEDIATES COMPARISON

• Carbocations (R⁺): 6 valence e⁻, sp² planar (120°), Electrophile. Stability: Tropylium > Ph₃C⁺ > Allyl ≈ Benzyl > 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺. Prone to 1,2-Hydride/Methyl shifts!
• Carbanions (R⁻): 8 valence e⁻, sp³ pyramidal (107°), Nucleophile. Stability: Allyl ≈ Benzyl > CH₃⁻ > 1° > 2° > 3° (Reversed!). No 1,2-shifts.
• Free Radicals (R•): 7 valence e⁻, sp² planar, Paramagnetic. Stability: Ph₃C• > Allyl ≈ Benzyl > 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃•. No 1,2-shifts.
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Carbocations ($\text{R}^+$)**: Electron-deficient (6 valence electrons, $sp^2$ planar with vacant $p$-orbital). Stabilized by $+I$, $+M$, and hyperconjugation. Readily undergo **1,2-hydride and 1,2-methyl rearrangements** to form more stable $3^\circ$ ions.
2. **Carbanions ($\text{R}^-$)**: Electron-rich (8 valence electrons, $sp^3$ pyramidal with lone pair). Stabilized by $-I$, $-M$, and $s$-character. Stability order is **reversed**: $\mathbf{\text{CH}_3^- > 1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ}$. Do NOT rearrange.
3. **Carbon Free Radicals ($\text{R}^\bullet$)**: Neutral, 7 valence electrons, paramagnetic. Stabilized by hyperconjugation and resonance: $\mathbf{\text{Ph}_3\text{C}^\bullet > 3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ > \text{CH}_3^\bullet}$.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CARBOCATION 1,2-METHYL SHIFT

Neopentyl Carbocation (1°, Unstable):
(CH₃)₃C-CH₂⁺ ──[1,2-CH₃ Shift]──► (CH₃)₂C⁺-CH₂CH₃ (2-Methyl-2-butyl Carbocation, 3°, Highly Stable)
conceptBreakdown.content: Carbocations undergo spontaneous intramolecular rearrangements if a more stable carbocation can be produced via a 1,2-shift (*e.g., Neopentyl $1^\circ$ carbocation undergoes 1,2-methyl shift to form stable $3^\circ$ 2-methyl-2-butyl carbocation*).

quickRevision: Carbocations have 6 valence electrons and undergo 1,2-shifts.
Carbanions have 8 valence electrons and do NOT undergo 1,2-shifts.
Tropylium cation (C₇H₇⁺) is aromatic and exceptionally stable.
